L15: # UC Davis CAR-T trial for canine connective tissue cancers
L16: 
L17: 【11†Jackie Lochridge 🖊🐾】
L18: 
L19: 1w
L20: A new CAR-T trial at 【12†UC Davis Weill School of Veterinary Medicine】, led by 【13†Colorado State University】, for connective tissue cancers is enrolling dogs with external sarcomas. This trial is not placebo controlled, as the primary goals are to establish efficacy and safety in a larger pool of patients (this type of CAR-T cell has been tested in 5 dogs so far). This is particularly interesting given the recent pauses in CAR-T trials by Novartis and Bristol Myers Squibb on the human side.

L30: 🔬 Rivalta Test in Feline Medicine 🐈 Ever wondered what happens when an effusion meets the Rivalta test? The Rivalta test is a simple in-clinic test performed on body effusion and can provide valuable supportive evidence when Feline Infectious Peritonitis (FIP) is suspected. 🧪 Positive: The drop maintains its shape and slowly sinks like a “jellyfish.” 💧 Negative: The drop rapidly disperses into the solution.
L31: Positive Rivalta test is a supportive finding in suspected FIP, it should be interpreted alongside the clinical signs, effusion analysis, CBC/biochemistry, imaging, and other diagnostic tests. 🩺 One simple test. L41: Lab Limelight ⚕️ 🔬 Introducing the Cancer Plasticity and Phenotypic Modeling Lab Led by Dr. Jacob Cawley, the Cancer Plasticity and Phenotypic Modeling Lab is pioneering a transformative approach to cancer research. The lab focuses on understanding how cancer cells adapt and reorganize to form tissues, aiming to develop precise biomarkers and therapies that target gene regulation.
L42: By studying the inherent plasticity of cells—their ability to change gene activity in response to stimuli—the team seeks to unravel the complexities of cancer development and progression. A key area of their research is hemangiosarcoma, an aggressive cancer in dogs and a rare but deadly form in humans.
L43: The lab leverages insights into angiogenesis and blood vessel development to explore how hemangiosarcoma-specific plasticity can be redirected, potentially preventing catastrophic bleeding events associated with the disease. Through this innovative work, Dr. Cawley and his team aim to redefine cancer treatment, offering new hope for pets and people alike.

L53: Atrial standstill is an uncommon but important cause of marked bradycardia in dogs and cats. The key ECG clue is the absence of P waves with a slow escape rhythm — but a P-wave-free bradycardia should not be labelled atrial standstill automatically. Hyperkalemia must be excluded, and persistent cases should be interpreted together with echocardiography and evidence of absent atrial mechanical activity. In transient atrial standstill, correcting the underlying cause may restore atrial activity.
L54: In persistent symptomatic disease, permanent pacing is often the definitive treatment. This is a practical overview of the ECG pattern, differential considerations, work-up and treatment approach. 【27†#VeterinaryCardiology】 【28†#ECG】 【29†#AtrialStandstill】 【30†#Cardiology】 【17†#VeterinaryMedicine】

L62: The 2026 Veterinary Cancer Society Annual Conference has been a great event, with more to come tomorrow.
L63: Given my interest in autologous cancer vaccines (ACV), it is exciting to see how this area has grown: - Ardent Animal Health presented data from a prospective multicenter randomized clinical trial treating dogs with osteosarcoma evaluating their ACV and checkpoint inhibitor (CD200) - The team at Tufts is investigating an ACV with combination checkpoint inhibitor therapy to treat dogs with metastatic osteosarcoma - Researchers at University of Illinois are developing a dendritic cell ACV for dogs with osteosarcoma.
L64: - An increasing number of companies with ACV technology were represented in the exhibition hall: ELIAS Animal Health, Ardent Onco, and Vaxkit

L72: We are showcasing a promising step forward for cartilage regeneration in animals and people. 🐎💡 In partnership with 【13†Colorado State University】, SRF conducted an equine study of Dr. Stone’s cartilage repair technique, with the goal of making regeneration more effective, reproducible, and accessible for veterinary and human patients. Together with our collaborators, Drs.
L73: David Frisbie, 【33†Brad Nelson】, Katie Seabaugh, and 【34†Laurie Goodrich】, we are advancing our innovative surgical technique, Articular Cartilage Paste Graft (ArtCart), into its next generation, ArtCart+. ArtCart is our novel one-step procedure that uses a patient's own cartilage, bone, and stem cells to regrow joint surfaces after trauma and treat arthritis.
L74: This research aims to deliver this new, enhanced therapy to veterinarians by 2030, enabling them to treat arthritis in horses and other large animals more effectively, while helping pave the way toward an FDA-regulated human clinical trial. We’re thrilled to share this progress with our SRF community.
